headline: Highest risk is medium: MemMachine’s MCP/allowlisted egress can amplify prompt injection, leakage, and cascading errors when paired with a local game agent that lacks isolation.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: MemMachine exposes an MCP Server and REST/Python SDK, so it can ingest external content through shared channels; godot_rl_agents has no isolation or communication surfaces documented, so a bridge is plausible but not proven. The pairwise pathway is inferred from docs only, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF MemMachine receives attacker-controlled content through its MCP Server or REST API and forwards it into prompts
IF godot_rl_agents is connected via a shared workspace, clipboard, or MCP bridge
mitigations: Disable MCP access for untrusted sources
Separate the agents into distinct workspaces
Add provenance tags to all cross-agent messages
Require manual review before any content from MemMachine is reused
requires-engineering: add input sanitization and instruction-stripping at the bridge

B_data_leakage.rationale: MemMachine touches long-term user facts and conversational context and can egress over allowlisted network paths; godot_rl_agents shows no data-touching surface, but the pair can still leak if MemMachine exports context or summaries. Because the interaction is undocumented, this is inferred rather than directly evidenced, so medium is the safer choice.
conditions: IF MemMachine sends conversation context or memory records to its allowlisted egress destination
IF any shared workspace or API payload contains user facts that are later surfaced by godot_rl_agents
mitigations: Restrict MemMachine egress to approved endpoints only
Avoid placing sensitive notes in shared files
Redact user facts before cross-agent transfer
Review outbound payloads for memory fields
requires-engineering: enforce per-field data-loss prevention

C_capability_conflict.rationale: godot_rl_agents is documented as network-egress none, while MemMachine has allowlisted egress and MCP/API surfaces, so their write domains do not obviously overlap. No shared filesystem, git, or database write capability is documented for either agent, making direct conflict unlikely and limited to unusual orchestration.
conditions: IF an orchestrator grants both agents write access to the same mutable resource
IF MemMachine is configured to write into a workspace that godot_rl_agents also mutates
mitigations: Keep separate output directories
Disable shared mutable mounts
Serialize writes through one coordinator
Use file locks for any shared artifact
requires-engineering: add optimistic-concurrency checks

D_cascading_error.rationale: MemMachine is explicitly an agentic travel-planning system with MCP/API interfaces, so it may treat upstream outputs as actionable context; godot_rl_agents can generate outputs that MemMachine could consume. The pairwise chain is plausible but not directly documented, so the safer assessment is medium rather than low.
conditions: IF MemMachine consumes godot_rl_agents output without verification
IF godot_rl_agents produces recommendations that MemMachine turns into downstream actions or messages
mitigations: Insert a verification step before reuse
Mark godot_rl_agents output as untrusted
Require human approval for downstream actions
Log source attribution on every reused claim
requires-engineering: add schema validation between agents

E_compliance.rationale: MemMachine touches long-term user facts and conversational context, which can create retention or subject-rights obligations; godot_rl_agents is a game-playing open-source project with no data classes touched, so it is not the compliance driver here. No residency or certification mismatch is documented, so this is a limited policy-gap risk only.
conditions: IF MemMachine retains user facts longer than the operator’s policy allows
IF the deployment stores conversational context in a jurisdiction with stricter retention rules
mitigations: Review retention settings
Delete stale memory records
Export a data inventory
Limit stored user facts to minimum necessary
requires-engineering: align residency and deletion workflows
